name: Fictiv
how_read: Plain HTTPS page fetch, robots.txt checked first, no account, no upload, no quote; figures copied as published. Prose quotes are verbatim; 'table_row' quotes name the table, row and cells (verified cell by cell); repository quotes are verbatim.
not_read: Re-fetching https://www.fictiv.com/specifications/cnc-machining, /specifications, /specifications/3d-printing, /capabilities/* and the CNC design-guide article on 2026-11-19 returned HTTP 403 (a Cloudflare challenge; robots.txt allows Claude-User). Not retried or worked around. The CNC specification page as fetched earlier the same day (plain fetch, for the sheet-metal rules) is the source; no Fictiv 3D-printing figures were read.

rules.note: Evaluated here: the cutter is taken as the largest that fits the pocket (its width, and twice its corner radius). The same rule in mechloop/data/supplier_rules/fictiv.json is kept as not evaluated.
rules.quote: Avoid deep pockets and cavities (max depth = 4x tool diameter)

rules.note: Engraved and embossed text is not extracted from the model (gap).
rules.quote: Avoid small text and logos (min 0.020″ depth, 0.030″ width)
Consolidate features to one side when possible – reduces setups from 4-6 down to 2-3, saving 30-90 min per part
Avoid undercuts requiring T-slot cutters or lollipop mills – these add 15-45 min programming + specialized tooling costs
Standard tolerances (±0.005" / ±0.127mm) are achievable with normal machining.
